newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss name experts on plan for SNB legal changes.
newsitem.headline: Swiss name experts on plan for SNB legal changes.

text.p: The Swiss National Bank (SNB) and the Swiss Federal Finance Ministry named a group of experts on Thursday to draft a master plan for revising SNB laws.
Reforms to allow the SNB to make more efficient use of its assets have been considered for some time.

The reforms drew international attention in March when the Swiss government proposed using gold which would be freed up by the planned changes to form the basis for a seven billion Swiss franc humanitarian fund.
The fund was created following interational criticism about Swiss banks' ties to the Nazi government in World War Two.

The planned changes, including using gold to form the fund, cannot be implemented until the constitutional reforms are completed. The Swiss cabinet meanwhile wants to have a formal plans for the fund this autumn.

According to an updated article 89 of the draft Constitution now on the table, the SNB will be required to provide adequate currency reserves to back notes in circulation, replacing a requirement that the notes be backed with gold and foreign exchange holdings.
The working group will examine the impact of plans to end the link between the Swiss franc and gold.
It will also prepare a rule for valuing the remaining gold which the SNB will continue to hold when the reforms are implemented.
The group's co-chairmen are Ulrich Gygi, director of the Swiss finance ministry, and Peter Klauser, an SNB director.
The 10-member group also includes SNB chief economist Georg Rich, as well as university professors and finance ministry officials.
